answer: Proposed biosecurity gate: each ID/day funds one DNA assay of a distinct assigned falcon, garden pest or ivory sample. A trusted lab signs ID/day, sample and spent-cartridge serials; the registry checks signatures and nonreuse, denying listing on failure. Cartridges and fees recur; analyzers are reusable capital; no stake. Lab collusion can fake delivery; bulk discounts lower costs, and owner uniqueness is unproved. With honest labs, ten IDs need ten single-use cartridges and assays; sharing analyzers or running in parallel cannot reduce that count.
